conviction_note: Halma's half-year results have moved the stock hard. The last two moved +5.7% and +9.2%, each with a guidance upgrade, and the FY26 results fell 15.4% on the photonics guide. This period was only partly pre-released: the 24 Sep trading update raised the FY27 EBIT margin guide to 23.5-24% but gave no H1 numbers. So abs_move is 6.5. p_up is only 55, because the margin raise is already in the company-compiled consensus (FY 23.7%) and the stock fell 2.2% on that trading update. The only directional evidence is counterparty proxies (Lumentum OCS shipments doubling, Alphabet 2027 capex rising), and these cut both ways: they read as demand for Avo's optical switches and as a share threat at the hyperscaler. The findings sum +0.6 and the scaled number is +0.65. The two agree because both rest on the same weak lean.

already_public.what: Scheduled H1 trading update: 'strong progress in the first half'. FY27 organic cc revenue growth guide reiterated at low double digit, including c.5pp photonics premium (photonics c.30% organic growth). FY27 adjusted EBIT margin guide raised to 23.5%-24% from c.22.7%. Order intake ahead of revenue and of the prior year. FX translation negative, c.-£8m revenue and c.-£2m profit at GBP/USD 1.35 and GBP/EUR 1.17. £515m invested in six acquisitions; three disposals realised c.£83m. Results date 19 Nov 2026 confirmed.

Company-compiled consensus, 12-14 analysts updated 24 Sep-9 Oct 2026. HY26/27: revenue £1,426.5m, adjusted EBIT £332.3m (23.3% margin), adjusted EPS 63.0p, DPS 10.2p. FY26/27: revenue £2,977.5m, adjusted EBIT £705.1m (23.7% margin, the midpoint of the raised guide). FY27/28: revenue £3,276.5m, adjusted EBIT £771.7m.

FY26 results: revenue £2.58bn (+15%), adjusted EBIT £594.5m. One hyperscaler customer (Avo Photonics, optical switches) was 20% of group revenue, up from 15%. The FY27 photonics premium was guided to c.5pp from c.8pp and the stock fell c.15%.

new_in_release.expect: First H1 numbers: organic growth rate, photonics H1 growth, H1 margin. Probably at or slightly above the £332.3m EBIT consensus, given the September margin raise. Mildly positive.

FY27 revenue guide (low double digit) could move to the upper end or be raised, as at H1 in 2024 and 2025. The margin guide was already raised in September, so a further margin raise is less likely. Lean up, uncertain.
Photonics commentary: FY27 c.30% growth held or raised, and any read on FY28 hyperscaler demand. This is the stock's central debate and the largest single swing, direction unknown.
Net debt will rise after the record £515m of M&A (Dreampath £238m, Pyxis £148m), and H1 cash conversion has run below the 90% KPI before. Unknown, a modest downside risk.
Interim DPS consensus is 10.2p against 9.63p, about +6%, in line with the 47-year growth record. Neutral.
Order intake was ahead of revenue at the trading update, so H2 commentary is likely constructive. Unknown.

findings.finding: Two counterparty signals since the 24 Sep trading update read through to Avo Photonics' optical-switch demand at its hyperscaler customer (20% of group revenue). Lumentum reported on 2 Nov that OCS shipments are ramping and 'OCS demand visibility has expanded significantly in recent months'. Alphabet held 2026 capex at $195-205bn on 28 Oct and said capex will rise significantly in 2027. Together these support the c.30% FY27 photonics growth guide being held or raised and a constructive FY28 read. They also flag a competing OCS supplier ramping in the same market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The photonics guide is what moves this stock. FY26 results fell 15.4% when the photonics premium was guided down from 8pp to 5pp. The 24 Sep 2026 trading update left photonics unchanged and the stock closed -2.2% despite the margin raise. The H1 2025/26 guidance upgrade, which included photonics, closed +9.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Both are public and widely read, so this is only partly unpriced. Halma's price did not respond: it fell from 3,500p (2 Nov) to 3,314p (5 Nov, -3.6% on about 3x normal volume) and sits near its 22 Oct 52-week low of 3,256p, about 30% below the pre-FY level of 4,878p. That is not what a market extrapolating the counterparty strength into Halma's photonics guide would show. The market appears to read Lumentum as a share threat, so the sign is genuinely open.
findings.independence: Alphabet Q3 2026, 28 Oct (a different source, the direct customer): capex guide held at $195-205bn with a significant increase in 2027 (https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2026/10/28/google-misses-revenue-expectations-alphabet-stock-sinks-in-early-after-hours-trading). TrendForce on Google Apollo OCS scaling (https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260210-12919.html).

findings.finding: Sterling has moved since the 24 Sep FX assumption. GBP/USD is 1.317 against the assumed 1.35, which helps the c.48% US revenue base. GBP/EUR is 1.199 against 1.17, which hurts the c.19% European base. The net translation effect is likely slightly less negative than the guided c.-£8m revenue and c.-£2m profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to the FX line on this name. The trading update flagged FX and the stock closed -2.2%, a move driven by photonics, not FX.
findings.why_not_priced: Any analyst can compute it, so it is mostly priced. The consensus was collated 24 Sep-9 Oct, partly before the dollar strengthened in November (GBP/USD 1.337 on 2 Nov, 1.317 on 18 Nov), so an FX update in the release could nudge the guide by a few £m. Too small to move a £12bn stock by itself.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print de-rated: 3,428p against 4,878p before the FY results and a 52-week low of 3,256p on 22 Oct. The forward P/E is about 25x, down from a historical sector premium of 50% to 35% (ii, Sep). The company-compiled consensus already embeds the raised margin. An in-line H1 with photonics held clears a lowered bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From a de-rated start, the H1 prints of 2024 (+5.7%) and 2025 (+9.2%) rallied on upgrades. The 2026 trading update (-2.2%) shows an upgrade alone is not enough.
findings.why_not_priced: This largely is the price, overlapping the free control (60d run-up -4.1%). It is filed small and only because expectations reset lower lean the reaction function slightly toward relief on an in-line print.
findings.independence: ii view on the trading update: forward P/E about 25x, premium down from 50% (https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/ii-view-halma-now-more-optimistic-about-annual-profits-ii540380)

baseline_tension: The priced lean is about 0 (-0.08) with no disclosed short, and the 5d (-3.8%) and 60d (-4.1%) run-ups are negative. The small positive lean found here mildly cuts against recent tape weakness, and it rests on counterparty proxies that the tape itself appears to have read as negative.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic-UK sources (the Investegate RNS originals, Halma's own consensus page and the ii/AJ Bell retail write-ups) supplied the primary documents and the company-compiled consensus, but no information absent from the wire and international coverage.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance change median 9.0%): this period was not pre-released in numbers and Halma has upgraded at H1 two years running, so abs_move_pct went from 5.5 to 6.5. p_up stays at 55.
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with': the de-rating finding overlaps the free control (60d run-up), cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

'A narrow proxy loses' and coverage above 13 analysts: the Lumentum/Alphabet read-through is a proxy on a 14-16 analyst name and cuts both ways (demand versus competitor share), cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': added cash_flow/net debt as a new_in_release risk line after record M&A. No source-backed number, so no finding.
